title: U.S. Labor Department Launches Sweeping H-1B Visa Fraud Probe With Dozens of Subpoenas
excerpt: Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito says investigators are issuing subpoenas and preparing search warrants as the Trump administration's anti-fraud task force targets employment-based visa programs used heavily by Indian IT firms.
body:
• The Department of Labor's Inspector General launched a major investigation into H-1B and PERM visa fraud on July 8, issuing dozens of subpoenas to companies and labor brokers.
  • Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito named IT firm Cognizant as part of the probe's "chatter" based on whistleblower concerns, though no formal charges have been filed.
  • Indian nationals receive roughly 70% of all approved H-1B petitions, making the crackdown a high-stakes issue for the diaspora community.
  • The probe comes as Microsoft laid off 1,600 Xbox workers while holding approval for 2,273 new H-1B visas, fuelling bipartisan anger over the program.

Federal Investigators Move Aggressively

The U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Inspector General has launched what it calls the most aggressive action against foreign labor fraud in the administration's history. Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito announced on July 8 that investigators had already begun issuing dozens of subpoenas to companies and labor brokers suspected of manipulating the H-1B and PERM visa systems.

https://x.com/FAIRImmigration/status/2079212781706818021

"We are going to make sure that we track down every lead," D'Esposito said, according to the New York Post. The Department of Labor is working alongside the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security as part of Vice President JD Vance's White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, established by executive order in March.

"This isn't just paperwork fraud — it's the exploitation of vulnerable workers, forced labor, the displacement of American workers, and abusive human trafficking. My top priorities are exposing fraud, protecting American workers, and putting criminals in cuffs."

— Anthony D'Esposito, Inspector General, U.S. Department of Labor

The investigation forms part of Project Firewall, a multi-agency initiative launched in September 2025 to increase oversight of employment-based visas. Since then, the Labor Department has opened more than 175 investigations into visa program abuses, according to VisaVerge.

Cognizant Named, Microsoft Controversy Intensifies

D'Esposito singled out IT consulting giant Cognizant on July 9, saying whistleblowers had raised the company's name in discussions about alleged PERM and H-1B abuses. He did not accuse Cognizant of wrongdoing and no formal charges have been announced. Cognizant is among the largest users of H-1B visas alongside Amazon, Infosys, IBM, and Microsoft.

The investigation gained political fuel when Microsoft's Xbox gaming division laid off roughly 1,600 employees while the parent company held approval for 2,273 H-1B visas this fiscal year. The juxtaposition drew fierce criticism from both Republican lawmakers and labor advocates.

Rep. Riley Moore, a West Virginia Republican, told Fox News that the H-1B program is "a scam" that has "been perpetrated on the American worker for far too long." Moore said a growing number of Republican colleagues privately support abolishing the program entirely.

What the Crackdown Means for Indian Workers

The stakes are especially high for Indian professionals. Data from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services shows that Indian nationals receive approximately 70% of all approved H-1B petitions. There are currently about 730,000 H-1B holders in the United States, with 65% working at technology companies, according to USCIS figures cited by the New York Post.

The administration has already reshaped the H-1B landscape in several ways. A wage-based selection system replaced the traditional random lottery on February 27, 2026, favouring higher-paid applicants and disadvantaging entry-level professionals. A proposed $100,000 H-1B application fee was struck down by a federal court in June 2026, though the administration has said it will appeal.

Starting July 10, USCIS began rejecting applications filed with auto-generated or copy-pasted signatures — a rule change that adds another compliance hurdle for employers and immigration attorneys.

The probe has also drawn attention to the L-1 intracompany transfer visa. Bloomberg reported earlier this year that former Tata Consultancy Services employees alleged the company secured more than 6,500 L-1A visa approvals between 2019 and 2023 by classifying technical and sales staff as managers. TCS has said it complies with federal law.

A Shifting Enforcement Model

Beyond the immediate investigation, the administration has moved from complaint-driven reviews to proactive "Secretary-certified" audits. Under this model, the Secretary of Labor can initiate audits based on reasonable cause alone, lowering the threshold for scrutiny. Companies now face unannounced site visits and online presence reviews, with non-compliance risking removal from the H-1B program, civil penalties, and criminal charges.

"H-1B abuse isn't just about jobs. It's about whether young Americans still believe they have a fair shot at the American dream."

— Anthony D'Esposito, DOL Inspector General, via New York Post

The political environment is shifting rapidly. The H-1B debate first erupted in late 2024 as a fault line between Trump-aligned tech leaders who backed the program and the MAGA base eager to restrict immigration. That tension has only deepened.

What to Watch

The investigation remains in its early stages. D'Esposito's office is preparing affidavits to seek search warrants, and the broad use of subpoenas signals an expanding review that could reach major employers, IT staffing intermediaries, and recruiting pipelines. For the roughly 500,000 Indian-origin H-1B holders, the outcome will determine not just job security but green card timelines and long-term immigration prospects. The administration's appeal of the struck-down $100,000 fee could further reshape the economics of skilled immigration to the United States.
